title: An Egyptian Empire
objective: After this level you can explain how Egypt built an empire in the New Kingdom.
summary: After the Hyksos, New Kingdom kings built buffer zones in Nubia and Canaan that grew into an empire, reaching the Fourth Cataract and the Euphrates.

cards.headline: Egypt had learned a hard lesson: trouble next door can end up on your throne.
cards.body: Ahmose understood that the Hyksos had grown strong because earlier kings let them. So the New Kingdom’s pharaohs set out to keep the next threat a long way from home.

cards.headline: Buffer zones
cards.body: After the Hyksos were gone, Ahmose and the kings after him pushed Egypt’s borders outward, creating buffer zones: Nubia to the south, Canaan to the north. Later pharaohs, above all Thutmose III, grew those buffers into an empire. Think of a moat, except the moat is made of other countries.
cards.callout: Keep enemies far away, then keep what you took

cards.headline: Past the rapids
cards.body: Remember the First Cataract, the rapids at Aswan that marked Egypt’s southern border in Level 5? New Kingdom armies went far beyond it. Egypt conquered all of Nubia and held the Nile as far as the Fourth Cataract. The prize was gold from the Nubian deserts, and Egypt ran the region through viceroys who oversaw the collection of tribute.

cards.headline: To the Euphrates
cards.body: In the north, Thutmose I campaigned through Syria as far as the Euphrates River. For kings whose whole world had been one river valley, that was quite a road trip. A kingdom built on the Nile now touched a second great river, and Egypt was no longer just a country. It was an empire.

cards.headline: The empire: mapped
learned: Buffer zones in Nubia and Canaan kept threats far away
Later kings grew them into an empire
Egypt held Nubia to the Fourth Cataract, for its gold

questions.prompt: How far north did Thutmose I’s campaigns reach?

options.label: Only to the edge of the Sinai desert
options.rationale: He went much farther, through Syria.

options.label: The shores of the Black Sea
options.rationale: His campaigns stopped at a river, not a sea.

options.label: The Mediterranean island of Crete
options.rationale: His armies marched overland through Syria.

questions.explanation: Thutmose I campaigned through Syria as far as the Euphrates.

questions.prompt: Why did New Kingdom pharaohs push Egypt’s borders out into Nubia and Canaan?

options.label: To find new farmland for a growing population
options.rationale: The goal was security, not farmland.

options.label: To escape a failing Nile flood
options.rationale: Nothing here is about the flood.

options.label: To spread the worship of the Aten
options.rationale: The Aten’s moment came later, and it was about religion, not borders.

options.label: To keep threats like the Hyksos far from home

questions.explanation: Having lived under the Hyksos, the kings built buffer zones so the next threat would be far from Egypt.

questions.prompt: Level 5’s First Cataract once marked Egypt’s southern border. How far south did New Kingdom control reach?

options.label: No farther than the First Cataract
options.rationale: New Kingdom armies went well beyond it.

options.label: As far as the Fourth Cataract, deep in Nubia
To the Euphrates River
options.rationale: That was the northern limit, in Syria.

questions.explanation: Egypt conquered all of Nubia and held the Nile as far as the Fourth Cataract.
